title: terraform + helm: conditional controlplane endpoint IAM role, helm values migration, and safe upgrade pausepoint
author: Devon Park
release_notes: Added: conditional IAM role acceptance for controlplane PrivateLink endpoints; Added: Helm values migration shim and documentation; Added: cluster upgrade pausepoint that drains controlplane subnet attachments; Added: DNS orphan cleaner to remove stale private hosted-zones after endpoint teardown; Notes: migration includes a canary rollout path and an automated rollback hook.
description:
Motivation: customers running Private (VPC) control planes occasionally run into cross-account PrivateLink acceptance failures when the control plane account doesn't have an explicit role surfaced by their infra account. We need a safer, opt-in way for operators to allow cross-account endpoint acceptance without widening default permissions. At the same time, we're changing some Helm values for the controlplane chart (TLS rotation config and endpoint annotations) and need a migration path to avoid disruption during upgrades. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: (1) a conditional IAM role in the terraform module for controlplane endpoints with explicit trust policy and a well-scoped assume-role for the installer account (opt-in via module variable controlplane_endpoint_iam_enabled=false by default), (2) a Helm values migration shim and docs so existing installs can transition value names without manual edits, plus a canary rollout plan in the chart, and (3) an upgrade pausepoint that drains controlplane subnet attachments and runs a DNS orphan-cleaner post teardown to prevent stale private hosted zones from lingering. Changes are backwards compatible by default and guarded by flags so customers can opt into the new flow. Checklist:
- [x] Terraform module: add conditional iam role (variable + docs + acceptance tests)
- [x] Helm: add values aliasing shim and migration guide (docs/site)
- [x] Installer: add upgrade pausepoint (safe drain + readiness probes)
- [x] Add DNS orphan cleaner lambda + unit tests
- [x] Add e2e/canary job for staged helm rollout
- [x] Update RBAC docs for new optional role
- [x] Manual smoke test against a staging VPC (cross-account accept flow)

Implementation notes:
- terraform/modules/controlplane-endpoint/main.tf contains the role resource guarded by var.controlplane_endpoint_iam_enabled. When enabled the module creates an iam_role with minimal AssumeRolePolicy allowing the installer account to AcceptVpcEndpointConnections; policy statements are narrowly scoped to the endpoint ARNs produced by the module.
- helm/charts/controlplane introduces values.migration.aliases mapping to accept older keys; the chart performs value normalization in a pre-install hook and emits a migration logmap to Release notes.
- installer orchestrator adds a pausepoint during the upgrade flow (upgrade pipeline step: drain-controlplane-subnet) which cordons endpoint attachments in a deterministic order and retries accept operations with exponential backoff.
- dns/orphan-cleaner is a small lambda (Go) invoked post-endpoint-delete to scan for private hosted zones that match deleted endpoint tags and delete them after a grace window.

Testing: unit tests for policy generation, helm template tests for aliases, an integration run in staging where the installer performed a canary helm upgrade across two controlplane zones, and a cross-account acceptance test using a throwaway installer role. Backwards compatibility: default variables are conservative (features off) and helm migration shim only reads/writes values without changing behavior unless migration flag is set. Rollout plan: enable module flag in a single customer's staging account, follow canary helm rollout via the console, observe DNS and acceptance metrics, then flip var and schedule broader rollout. Links: internal linear ENG-3241, support ticket SUP-8742.

migration_plan: Phase 1: Keep features disabled by default. Ship module and chart changes behind flags.
Phase 2: Run canary helm upgrade in staging customers and monitor acceptance metrics for 48h.
Phase 3: Enable terraform flag for select customer staging accounts; verify IAM role creation and acceptance flow.
Phase 4: Gradual rollout across regions with rollback guard if DNS orphan metric increases.
Rollback: run installer upgrade with --rollback-migration which triggers helm pre-install to use previous value names and deletes any created IAM role and orphan-cleaner schedules.
